headline: India's government has asked banks to plan a sector-wide shift to quantum-safe security.
score_reason: Policy step reported through one outlet citing an unnamed official; no published directive has been seen.
importance_line: What changed: the finance ministry has asked banks to assess their vulnerability to future quantum attacks and start mitigation, which matters to bank customers' long-term data, but the detail rests on an unnamed official and no published directive has been seen.
summary: The Economic Times reports that India's government has asked banks to assess their vulnerability to future quantum computers and begin measures to reduce it, citing an official who did not want to be named. The official said each bank can prepare its own strategy but there should be common industry guidelines, and a working group under the chief of the State Bank of India is examining the question.
notes: ET text partly paywalled: synopsis and first paragraphs read. The pool item (The420.in, 8 Oct 2026 03:46 UTC) is later and adds a 2027 to 2029 timeline, an RBI committee and EU deadlines; those are not in the ET text read here, so not used. The420.in does not credit another outlet. The AI resilience framework named in the ET headline is not described in the text read, so it is left out of the summary.
